answer: A VRF beacon keeps the network a haven for honest agents: every identity must prove it is alive. Each epoch the beacon randomly picks 5% of identities; each must file a compute heartbeat, a VDF proof of its identity, in ten minutes. The draw is unpredictable, so N puppets must all stay online: 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 GPU-hours per epoch, while an honest agent spends under five cents. Missing a heartbeat freezes rewards and flags the identity, so a lagoon of idle puppets drains the attacker's budget. Like yarrow spreading by roots, reputation grows from steady work, not mass-produced copies.
